documents.text: ESG Readiness Assessment Guide | Ragunauth Ramsaroop Ragunauth Ramsaroop Public-value intelligence Free Tools Resources Topics Methodology Start here Practical guide ESG Readiness Assessment Guide How to use an ESG readiness assessment without turning it into a vanity score An ESG readiness assessment should expose gaps in evidence, accountability and management systems. It should not reward polished language or imply that one composite score establishes sustainability performance. Begin with governance. An organisation should be able to identify who owns each material issue, what evidence is reviewed, how decisions are escalated and which commitments have been approved. Then test operating evidence. Climate, environment, workforce, human rights, communities, ethics, supply chain and reporting should be assessed with documents, data and controls rather than aspiration alone. Low scores are useful when they trigger action. A readiness assessment becomes practical when each weak area has an owner, an evidence requirement, a measurable action and a review date. High scores also need challenge. Ask whether the evidence is current, whether controls work in practice, whether affected stakeholders would describe performance the same way and whether disclosed claims match operating reality. It is to make assumptions explicit enough for a user to identify the major operational sources that deserve better data and formal review. Start with a clear organisational and operational boundary. It is not a substitute for hourly load modelling, resource assessment, protection studies, thermal design or bankable engineering. Daily energy demand is only the starting point. Peak demand, load shape and the timing of consumption determine whether a system that looks adequate on annual energy can meet operational requirements. Solar capacity depends on resource and system losses. A screening model can divide daily energy by peak-sun hours and an efficiency allowance, but detailed design should use location-specific resource data and component performance. Battery sizing should distinguish usable energy from nominal capacity. Depth of discharge, round-trip efficiency, degradation, reserve requirements and inverter power all matter. For industrial and mining applications, resilience is as important as energy cost. Model generator interaction, black-start capability, maintenance strategy, critical loads and the consequences of shortfalls before investment approval. documents.text: Government Relations vs Lobbying | Ragunauth Ramsaroop Skip to content RR Ragunauth Ramsaroop Executive intelligence profile Profile Decision Brief Case Studies Perspectives Research Authority Engage Home / Perspectives Government relations · 1 August 2026 · 3 min read Why Government Relations Is Not Lobbying Both can involve asking government for an outcome. The difference is whether the work ends with the ask or builds an institutional relationship that survives people, elections and reorganisations. Government relations is often misunderstood as a softer label for lobbying. In practice, the disciplines overlap at moments but operate on different time horizons. Transactions versus institutions Lobbying is commonly organised around a specific decision. Government relations has to prepare for the next decision as well as the current one. The professional question is not only "Did we get the answer?" but also "Did the institution understand our position, trust our information and know how to work with us next time?" The relationship cannot belong to one contact A relationship built around a single official is fragile. A durable relationship belongs to the organisation and the institution. It depends on accurate submissions, predictable conduct, respect for process and continuity when personnel change. Access is useful. Institutional credibility is durable. Abstract or executive overview Water is simultaneously a human right, an ecological process, a productive input, a transport medium, a public-health service and a strategic asset. These roles are often analysed separately. That separation is increasingly inadequate. Water scarcity can reduce crop yields, constrain thermal and hydroelectric generation, interrupt semiconductor and mining operations, increase urban costs, alter shipping routes, weaken public health and transmit losses into banks, insurers and sovereign balance sheets. Floods and water pollution create a different but equally material set of economic disruptions. The relevant security question is therefore not whether a country or company has access to water in aggregate. It is whether water of the required quantity and quality is available at the required place and time, under institutions capable of allocating it through stress. Executive summary from the original paper The energy transition is often presented as a choice between technologies. documents.text: The Physical Limits of Artificial Intelligence | Ragunauth Ramsaroop Independent executive research · September 2026 The Physical Limits of Artificial Intelligence Energy, water, critical minerals and the infrastructure requirements of advanced AI and hypothetical superintelligence, 2026-2035. Ragunauth Ramsaroop · Georgetown, Guyana · Research cut-off: 25 September 2026 · 25-page research edition. Executive summary AI growth depends on physical infrastructure. The research examines electricity, grid connections, cooling, water, chips, minerals, finance, cybersecurity and public acceptance as one connected industrial system. Decision standard The paper separates observations, institutional projections, author calculations and hypothetical scenarios. documents.title: Sovereign AI
documents.description: Research on control, continuity, substitutability and assurance across the AI infrastructure stack.
documents.text: Sovereign AI | Ragunauth Ramsaroop Skip to content RR Ragunauth Ramsaroop Executive intelligence profile Profile Decision Brief Case Studies Perspectives Research Authority Engage Home / Research & Publications AI infrastructure research monograph · September 2026 Sovereign AI: Who Controls the Intelligence Infrastructure? A systems-level study of strategic control across compute, cloud, chips, data, models, energy, connectivity and institutional capability. Sovereignty is treated as durable control over critical outcomes and dependencies, not as a requirement for total technological self-sufficiency. Core definition The paper defines sovereign AI as the capacity to exercise durable, lawful and practical control over critical AI capabilities, data and operational choices. The test includes authority, continuity, substitutability, assurance and strategic choice. Strategic interdependence Domestic hosting alone does not guarantee sovereignty, and foreign infrastructure does not automatically remove it. The key question is whether dependencies are visible, governed, portable and replaceable within an acceptable time and risk envelope. System layers The research examines semiconductors, advanced compute, cloud concentration, electricity, data governance, model access, connectivity, cybersecurity, talent, public-sector capability and the legal conditions that shape operational control. Decision discipline The monograph argues against prestige-driven self-sufficiency. Institutions

documents.title: The Trust Deficit
documents.description: Research monograph on warranted institutional trust, governance, execution capacity and transformation in a fragmented world.
documents.text: The Trust Deficit | Ragunauth Ramsaroop Skip to content RR Ragunauth Ramsaroop Executive intelligence profile Profile Decision Brief Case Studies Perspectives Research Authority Engage Home / Research & Publications Global leadership research monograph · September 2026 The Trust Deficit Managing Transformation in a Fragmented World. The monograph treats warranted institutional trust as an operating condition for cooperation, reform and execution rather than as a communications score. Research proposition Institutions need enough warranted trust to coordinate difficult action under uncertainty while preserving scrutiny, contestability, lawful opposition, audit and correction. High trust is not treated as inherently good, and scepticism is not treated as failure. Why trust affects execution When institutional credibility deteriorates, coordination becomes more expensive. Stakeholders demand more proof, add safeguards, slow decisions and move transactions into defensive structures. The paper therefore links trust to execution capacity, reform durability and the ability to absorb shocks. Analytical framework The research separates interpersonal trust from institutional trust, reputation from legitimacy, popularity from credibility, transparency from disclosure volume, and technical capacity from execution capacity. It also proposes stress-testing institutions against shocks such as cyber incidents, policy reversals, model failures, supply interruptions and fiscal crises. Evidence

documents.text: Water Security as Economic Security | Executive White Paper Download full PDF: Water Security as Economic Security Â· All downloadable papers Skip to content RR Ragunauth Ramsaroop Executive intelligence profile Profile Decision Brief Case Studies Perspectives Research Authority Engage Home / Research & Publications Research monograph & strategic white paper · 20 September 2026 Water Security as Economic Security Water as a first-order variable linking food, power, industry, cities, finance, trade and national resilience. Research mandate The work integrates hydrology, public health, agriculture, energy, manufacturing, data-centre, trade and financial-risk evidence. It separates scarcity from service failure, withdrawals from consumption, and physical risk from governance risk. Analytical framework The research develops a twelve-domain Water Security Systems Framework, a Water Security Resilience Index concept and a Strategic Water Exposure Score for structured analysis of systems, assets and sectors. Strategic value The central proposition places water inside national economic strategy, corporate capital allocation and infrastructure planning rather than treating water as a narrow environmental topic. Evidence boundary The work is independent research with an evidence cut-off of 20 September 2026. Its frameworks are analytical tools and require local calibration before operational use.
